payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show any change to the mug’s position relative to the headphones?
node.criteria: pass: The mug’s position relative to the headphones visibly changed. fail: The mug’s position relative to the headphones visibly did not change. unknown: A change cannot be determined from the available images.
node.binding: Compare the original and edited images only to assess progress toward the requested relative-position change; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The mug’s position relative to the headphones visibly changed between the source and edited images; the edited image shows the mug on the headphones’ right.

fulfillment: The node’s yes decision is unsupported by the images: the edited image shows two mugs and a blurred mug-shaped remnant at the source location, while the headphones are also altered; the rightmost mug appears right of the headphones, but the trace does not establish that this is the original mug moved rather than a duplicate, nor whether the other changes count as requested progress. The source has one mug left of the headphones. Make the binding and criteria explicitly track the same mug across source and edit, and distinguish verified movement from mere final-state placement or duplication. Ensure the decision uses the rubric’s partial outcome when some requested progress is established but completion is not, and unknown when identity/progress cannot be resolved; do not infer completion from the two supporting checks alone. The high-confidence dependency reports conflict with visible image evidence, so improve evidence grounding and calibrate confidence rather than treating those reports as conclusive. No transport, schema, or dependency-execution failure is indicated.

Tighten the binding to compare the same source mug across images and assess its movement relative to the headphones; distinguish a verified move from a duplicate or an unrelated new object. Ground the decision in visible identity and positional evidence, and lower confidence or return unknown when those cannot be resolved rather than asserting progress from the rightmost mug’s placement alone. Keep the node’s progress judgment distinct from overall completion: this support check must not turn a partial edit into a yes/full-fulfillment conclusion, and unrelated changes do not count. The trace is an evidence-grounding/confidence problem, not a transport, schema, or dependency-execution failure."}
